top_signal.title: How do you scale when each batch doesn’t pay for the next one’s MOQ?
top_signal.summary: First-time founder with a physical product. My first batch of 500 units arrives soon, and I’m stuck on how scaling actually works.   The basics:     Landed cost is about $33.50/unit, retail is $89.99   MOQ is about 500 units   Lead time is about 4 months from order to warehouse     My problem is that after fees, shipping and ads, batch 1 won’t bring in enough to pay for a bigger batch 2. Then batch 2 won’t cover batch 3, and so on. Each batch only grows the cash a little, and with a 4-month wait in between, it feels like it would take years to get anywhere.   We’ve also put about $30k of our own money in so far. If every batch’s profit goes into the next order, especially as we add new SKUs, I’m not sure when we’d ever start paying ourselves back.   Our goal is to grow this into a business doing six figures in revenue, but I can’t see how to get there when each batch barely funds the next.   So for those who’ve scaled a physical product:     How did you pay for bigger batches when your sales couldn’t cover them yet?   When did you bring in outside money (loans, inventory financing, investors), and was it worth it?   How did you balance paying yourselves back with reinvesting in new inventory?   How did you handle MOQs when adding new products? Did you negotiate smaller runs, or launch fewer SKUs at first?   If you were starting over with a small budget, what would you do differently?     I’d really appreciate hearing what actually worked for you.       submitted by
